title: Creating a Bootable USB?
reason:
Tools like Rufus require raw block device access (e.g., /dev/sda). The Windows compatibility sandbox strictly isolates hardware access to prevent system corruption, causing these apps to crash.

For AnduinOS, we highly recommend Impression — a native, beautifully designed, and rock-solid tool for flashing disk images.

title: Checking Hardware & Benchmarks?
reason:
Windows hardware monitors require ring-0 access to read motherboard and NVMe sensors. The sandbox intentionally blocks these API calls.

For deep hardware inspection and real-time telemetry, please use Mission Center, the native system monitor for AnduinOS.

title: Managing Disk Space or File Transfers?
reason:
Running disk analyzers inside a Windows sandbox yields inaccurate results because it can only see the virtual 'C: Drive' mapped by Bottles, not your actual Ext4/Btrfs root filesystem.

Please use the native Disk Usage Analyzer for accurate storage telemetry.

title: Installing Visual Studio?
reason:
The full Visual Studio IDE relies heavily on deep Windows GUI frameworks (WPF/WPF) and MSBuild ecosystems that perform poorly under Wine.

For C# and .NET development on Linux, JetBrains Rider is the industry standard, offering native performance, a superior ReSharper engine, and perfect .NET SDK integration.

title: Installing Visual Studio Code?
reason:
Running the Windows build of VS Code means you lose access to the Linux native terminal, Docker socket, and Git ecosystem.

VS Code provides an excellent native Linux build. Please install it directly via the App Store.

title: Deploying Microsoft SQL Server?
reason:
Microsoft SQL Server has native, highly optimized binaries for Linux! Running the Windows installer through Wine is completely unnecessary and unsupported.

Click 'View Documentation' to learn how to deploy SQL Server natively on Linux or via Docker.

title: Installing Runtimes or SDKs?
reason:
Installing developer SDKs (like .NET, Go, Node.js, or PowerShell) inside the Windows sandbox will trap them there — your native Linux terminal and IDEs won't be able to find them.

These runtimes are natively supported on AnduinOS. Please install them via apt, Snap, or native tarballs.

title: Configuring IIS Web Server?
reason:
Internet Information Services (IIS) is deeply embedded into the Windows NT kernel and cannot run on Linux.

For modern, high-performance web routing and automatic HTTPS, we highly recommend migrating to Caddy or NGINX.

title: Installing Docker Desktop?
reason:
Container engines require low-level kernel modules which are inaccessible from the sandbox.

Please use native Podman or Docker Engine directly on your Linux host.

title: Installing Virtual Machines?
reason:
Hypervisors require hardware virtualization (VT-x/AMD-V) which is inaccessible from the sandbox.

For virtual machines, we highly recommend GNOME Boxes.

title: Media & Creative Tools
reason:
Media tools like OBS, Blender, and VLC require low-level NVENC/NVDEC hardware encoders, Vulkan API, or ALSA audio routing. Running their Windows versions adds a massive overhead.

All of these applications provide flawless, GPU-accelerated native Linux versions. Please fetch them from the App Store.

reason:
The Adobe CC installer utilizes complex anti-piracy DRM and proprietary MSVCP libraries that frequently deadlock the compatibility layer.

We recommend maintaining a Windows dual-boot or virtual machine for heavy Adobe workflows, or migrating to Linux-native tools like DaVinci Resolve and Krita.

title: Installing CPU-Z?
reason: CPU-X is a native Linux application that perfectly mirrors CPU-Z in functionality and interface, without the need for Windows sandboxing.

title: Looking for a Download Manager?
reason: Windows downloaders often encounter network routing issues inside the sandbox. We recommend Motrix, a beautiful, full-featured native Linux download manager.

title: Looking for a Torrent Client?
reason: Windows torrent clients can't properly optimize network connections inside a sandbox. We highly recommend qBittorrent, a powerful native Linux client.

title: Installing QQ or TIM?
reason: Tencent now officially maintains a natively built Linux QQ based on the NT architecture. It provides an identical experience to the Windows version without the overhead of Wine.

title: Installing Postman?
reason: API tools run much more efficiently with direct access to your native network stack. Please install the native Linux version of Postman.

title: Installing a Password Manager?
reason: Password managers require deep system integrations (like clipboard access and browser extensions) that are intentionally blocked by the Windows sandbox for security reasons. Please use the native Linux version.

title: Installing GitHub Desktop?
reason: A highly stable, community-maintained native Linux build of GitHub Desktop is available. It integrates flawlessly with your native Git ecosystem.

title: Installing HandBrake?
reason: Video transcoding requires direct access to hardware encoding (like NVENC or QuickSync) and massive multi-core CPU performance. The native Linux version provides vastly superior speeds.
